newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta Wheat Pool plans more elevators for export.
newsitem.headline: Alberta Wheat Pool plans more elevators for export.

text.p: Canada's second largest grain handler plans to build more large capacity elevators as it expects much of Canada's western Prairie crop to continue to be exported, Alberta Wheat Pool president Alex Graham said.

"I think there'll be a pull on grains for either domestic use or exports, but I expect we'll see more processing on the eastern Prairies with more grains and oilseeds exported from the western Prairies," Graham told Reuters in an interview.
The amount of grain Alberta Wheat Pool (AWP) shipped in 1996/97 (Aug/July) rose to 5.9 million tonnes from 5.5 million tonnes the year before.
AWP expected to ship 6.4 million tonnes in the past crop year, but a wet fall and early, heavy snowfall in the Peace River Valley cut output by 500,000 tonnes, Graham said.
The farmer-owned cooperative raised C$100 million in fiscal 1995/96 in a long-term debt offer for capital projects.
It is building seven high-throughput elevators and plans to build at least two more, he said.

"We have sufficient funds to proceed on our projects," Graham said. "With the construction of larger facilities on the Prairies we'll be more able to fill quarter, half to full (100 hopper car) trains."
AWP's elevators turned stock over an average six times in 1996/97. The firm operated slightly more than 200 elevators after cutting 60 smaller elevators in the last 18 months, Graham said.
Revenues from AWP's grain businesses rose eight percent to C$2.3 billion in 1996/97 from C$2.13 billion.
While much of Alberta's production was expected to be exported, growth in livestock output should draw more feed grains to Alberta feed lots, he said.
"Alberta's a large consumer of feed grains in beef, pork, chicken and dairy. There will continue to be demand," he said.
Alberta had 40 percent of Canada's cattle and calves in 1996, or 5.94 million of the 14.89 million national herd.
Alberta also had 16 percent of Canada's pig herd, or 1.73 million of the 11.04 million national herd, Statistics Canada's 1996 census data shows.
There were 9.49 million hens and chickens in Alberta in 1996 out of a national total of 102.26 million.
A Taiwanese firm is building a pork packing plant in Lethbridge on forecasts hog output will rise in coming years, he said.
